$comment: Shared parity fixture (ADR-008, design.md D2). Hand-maintained: edit this file directly. Format and runners: parity/README.md. Never delete a case to make CI green.

cases.note: The :<exe> suffix is SDK-version dependent (R5): Python 1.42 has none.
Python sdk >= 1.45 ships a default service.instance.id detector (D4).
Pre-fork model: setup in each forked worker (gunicorn post_fork). Go has no pre-fork server model.
Valid secret header + a helper-warned trigger (bogus protocol); asserted on helper diagnostics only (R8: SDK messages are out of scope).

Portless gRPC URL triggers the D1.b warning; helper diagnostics must not print userinfo/query. A3 must also strip userinfo from gRPC endpoints before passing them to the SDK (R8). The all-channel `log` assertion becomes satisfiable only once A3 strips userinfo (SDK export-failure messages print the endpoint).
Warning text must recommend an explicit port (design D1.b).

Negative: schemeless gRPC is legal per spec; only http/protobuf schemeless is deprecated (D8). All channels: no diagnostic about the endpoint at all (a deprecation warning must name the variable, R8). helper_log checks the schemeless deprecation wording (shared by Go and Python), not any 'deprecat': the Python SDK emits an unrelated LoggingHandler DeprecationWarning and, with SQLAlchemy installed, the Python helper warns that the implicit SQL default is deprecated (A9).
Unparseable boolean: warn and use the default (enabled).

An explicit :80 on a gRPC http:// URL is kept: the target is <host>:80 over plaintext. WHATWG URL drops a scheme-default port (URL.host), which would make the Node gRPC exporter dial 443 (Node design D-JS3).

cases.requirement: R1/D1 edge-case rulings (2026-10-29, Node B4a refutation)
cases.note: Percent-encoding in the endpoint path is kept verbatim, never decoded (D1 ruling): the generic endpoint path /a%2Fb is sent as /a%2Fb/v1/<signal>, not /a/b/v1/<signal>. raw_path is the path as sent (fakeotlp records it). Go: the OTLP/HTTP exporters send url.URL.Path (decoded), see the D1 note "Go: path escapes decoded". Node: unit-tested until B4b.
{receiver_tls} serves TLS on 4317, so the D1.b default port is checked with TLS.
Needs the receiver on IPv6 loopback (FAKEOTLP_HOST_IPV6): skipped locally without it, fails under PARITY_REQUIRE_FAKEOTLP. Port 24318 keeps it apart from other tests.
Needs the receiver on IPv6 loopback (FAKEOTLP_HOST_IPV6): skipped locally without it, fails under PARITY_REQUIRE_FAKEOTLP. Port 24318 keeps it apart from other tests.
Neither library has a per-signal endpoint option yet; A3 adds it, maps `traces_endpoint` in both adapters and flips this to pass.
With no protocol set, the port-4318 inference for a signal uses that signal's endpoint.

Go passes since A2 only because of upstream credential precedence: the env CA (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE) wins over WithInsecure in all three gRPC exporters (otlploggrpc v0.7.0 ignored it and sent logs in plaintext; v0.23.0 honours it). The helper still does not resolve https + INSECURE=true: without a CA it exports plaintext (A3, D1.c).

Asserted via the grpc-timeout header (gRPC only; HTTP timeouts stay in A3 unit tests). Python: the SDK parses *_TIMEOUT as seconds while the spec says milliseconds (design D1.e); A3 adds the helper ms→s shim. Go: the SDK applies the env since A3 (G10: the helper passes no timeout unless set in code). Bound is lte 600, not 500: grpc encodes the remaining deadline and can round it up (501m observed with timeout=0.5 s passed by the helper); 600 still separates ms (500) from a seconds misread (500000) and the 10 s default (10000).

A span the handler starts under a health request must not be recorded either (D5: children follow the DROP).
A code option replaces the default health list (Go WithHealthPaths, design D5 'list overridable in code'); matching rules unchanged.

Go 0.2.0: the unary-server filter reads InterceptorInfo.Method, which otelgrpc v0.56 leaves empty for unary servers, so Check is traced (and counted). Since A7-go the D5 health sampler drops the span (the RPC is still counted).
R7: counted only where the instrumentation emits RPC metrics; Python contrib grpc emits none (documented gap, not a task).
otelgrpc v0.56 stream interceptors recorded no RPC duration metric; the v0.72 stats handler (A2) counts Watch in rpc.server.call.duration.

Design 'Mounted /metrics handler status': Prometheus deliberately not active answers 200 with an empty body (a 503 would mark the target up=0); 503 stays for before/failed/after-shutdown, covered by unit tests.

Design 'Mounted /metrics handler status': Prometheus deliberately not active answers 200 with an empty body (a 503 would mark the target up=0); 503 stays for before/failed/after-shutdown, covered by unit tests.
Go SDK New() rejects TLS config on an insecure HTTP endpoint; the helper drops the env TLS config for that signal and warns (design D1.c corollary).
Only tracecontext, baggage and none are supported (design D1 propagators row); other values warn and are skipped, leaving the default when nothing supported remains.
Precedence: code per-signal > code generic > env per-signal > env generic.
Scheme wins: http:// stays plaintext although a readable CA is set (Go SDK prefers env TLS credentials over Insecure).
Garbage per-signal timeout falls back to the generic one (ms). Bound 600: grpc-timeout carries the remaining deadline.
Zero is invalid: warn and use 10000 ms. Runners shut down with a ~5 s deadline, which caps the grpc-timeout seen on metrics/logs, hence gte 1000.
Valid pairs reach every signal; the malformed item is warned by position only. SDK messages (which echo the raw item) are out of scope, so redaction is asserted on helper_log.
Dedicated option wins in the resolved value and the emitted resource (A16).
Dedicated option wins in the resolved value and the emitted resource (A16).
A blank service.name in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES is not provided: the next level applies.
Blank service.name and nothing else: SDK default plus the warning.
A blank code resource_attributes service.name is not provided.

A blank deployment.environment.name is not provided: absent plus the ADR-003 warning. Go: the SDK providers' WithResource merges resource.Environment(), which re-adds the blank key as "" (D1 row "Go: SDK providers re-read OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES"; G7 forbids masking env).
A blank code deployment.environment.name is not provided: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES applies.
A blank service.instance.id is not provided: a per-process id is generated.
A blank code service.instance.id is not provided: a per-process id is generated.
Code-only resource_attributes service.name resolves to it, with no missing-name warning.
Helper-owned parsing: the item is skipped with a positional warning; the others are kept.
Blank items are ignored without a warning.
An invalid percent sequence keeps the value literal, with a positional warning.
A decode that is not valid UTF-8 keeps the value literal, with a positional warning.
Values are trimmed with the contract set after percent-decoding.
An item with an empty key is skipped with a positional warning.

Malformed or undecodable items are reported by position; their text never reaches helper diagnostics or the process output. Go: the SDK providers re-parse the variable; the helper's scoped error-handler filter drops their echo (A16).
telemetry.sdk.* always come from the SDK: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES values for them are ignored silently (A16).
telemetry.sdk.* always come from the SDK: code resource_attributes values for them are ignored, warned once naming the key (A16).

Keys are trimmed with the contract set only: a leading U+00A0 stays part of the key, and no trimmed duplicate appears. Go: the SDK providers' own parse (Unicode TrimSpace) adds the trimmed key (D1 Go row).
An empty (or trim-set-only) key in code resource_attributes is an invalid code value: setup fails naming the option (A16).

Detector-selection variables are not honored: no detector attributes, one warning naming the variable (Python OTEL_EXPERIMENTAL_RESOURCE_DETECTORS, Node OTEL_NODE_RESOURCE_DETECTORS). Go has no such variable (OTEL_GO_X_RESOURCE only gates the instance id).

A __proto__ key is an ordinary attribute (Node: own data property, never a prototype write). Node: the helper keeps it, but @opentelemetry/resources 3.0 Resource.attributes builds a plain object with attrs[k] = v, which drops __proto__ (D-JS14).
Propagator names are case-insensitive; Python crashed at import before A3 validation.
Empty tokens and a trailing comma are dropped.
A non-boolean INSECURE is false (warned); with http:// the scheme wins: plaintext.
Code insecure contradicting a code URL's scheme fails fast naming the option.
OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true: no SDK providers installed (the resource snapshot comes from the installed TracerProvider).
A parseable but rejected per-signal URL (empty host) falls back to the generic endpoint, which must actually receive the signal.
Schemeless per-signal endpoint; the per-signal INSECURE=false beats the generic INSECURE=true, so metrics use TLS.
Keys are not percent-decoded: x-parity%2Dk is outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] and skipped; the other pair is delivered.
A '/' in the password ends the authority for URL parsers; diagnostics must show <unparseable URL> or the host, never the password.
A '#' in the password starts a fragment for URL parsers.
An unparseable INSECURE warns even when no endpoint is configured (principle 8).
Per-signal variant of the INSECURE ruling.
A control character inside an opaque-scheme value makes it invalid (fall back to the generic endpoint), not an unsupported scheme.
Code variant: fails fast as a control-character error, not as an unsupported scheme.
An empty code otlp_protocol is not set (A13 ruling): env and defaults apply, no error.
An empty code compression is not set (A13 ruling). Node: the compression option lands in B4b.
A port above 65535 is invalid: warn <unparseable URL>, fall back.
Port 0 is outside 1-65535: invalid (WHATWG URL and Go accept it; Python treats it as no port).
Code variant: a port outside 1-65535 fails fast naming the option.
An unparseable endpoint is always shown as the constant, never as a host-less rendering.
Schemeless variant of the constant-rendering ruling (non-numeric port).
Code variant: the error names the option and shows the constant.

A port with thousands of leading zeros compares numerically (00…04318 = 4318, so the port-4318 inference applies) and never crashes the parser (Python int() refuses > 4300 digits).
UTS #46 non-transitional: a deviation character is kept (straße.de -> xn--strae-oqa.de, not strasse.de). Portless gRPC so the warning renders the host, as in endpoint.idn_host_punycoded.
A zero-width joiner outside its CONTEXTJ context fails IDNA: invalid. Env: warn <unparseable URL>, fall back to the generic endpoint.

An invalid %-escape in an http/protobuf path is invalid in every language (the Go exporters would fall back to their default endpoint; Python requests re-quotes every escape). Env: warn <unparseable URL>, fall back.
Code variant of the invalid path escape ruling: fail fast naming the option.
One host rule: a host that ends in a number must be a canonical dotted quad; 127.1 (WHATWG: 127.0.0.1, Go/Python: a DNS name) is invalid.
One host rule: an octet above 255 is invalid.
One host rule: an ASCII host must be an RFC 3986 reg-name ('{' is not one; WHATWG accepts it).
An opaque value renders as '<scheme>:' only: the text after the scheme may hold credentials.

No valid header item: the SDK must not re-parse the env var and echo it (Python masks it during exporter construction). Go: helper diagnostics pass (position only) but the OTel Go SDK's global logger echoes the raw value (parse headers) — out of the helper's control per the design D1 edge-case ruling on the SDK's own log output (G7 forbids masking env).
Valid decimal above 24 h is clamped to 24 h with a warning; the wire timeout must exceed the 10 s default (it is bounded by the runner's shutdown deadline).

The resolved timeout must bound the export beyond the SDK processors' own 30 s timeouts. Runners need a shutdown deadline above 60 s for this case. The metrics assertion checks only the exporter's grpc-timeout; the periodic reader's own deadline is covered by Go's TestPeriodicReaderUsesResolvedTimeout.
gte lowered 300→100 (2026-10-28): 212 ms observed under load; 100 still separates the 1 ms clamp from the 500 ms fallback.
gte lowered 300→100 (2026-10-28): 212 ms observed under load; 100 still separates the 1 ms clamp from the 500 ms fallback.
One invalid escape keeps the whole value literal (no partial decoding).
A tab inside the per-signal URL (host) makes it unparseable; traces fall back to the generic endpoint. Python's urlsplit would silently strip it.
A tab inside the port: unparseable, fall back to the generic endpoint.
A newline inside the path: unparseable, fall back to the generic endpoint + /v1/traces. The bad path differs from /v1/traces even with the control character stripped, so silent stripping cannot pass.
A value without // matching <scheme>:/ is an unsupported scheme: the signal is not exported (no fallback to the generic endpoint).
A13: a code value equal to the helper default still wins over the env ('was it set' is tracked, never compared to the default).
A13: code sample_ratio=1.0 wins over the deprecated OTEL_HELPER_SAMPLE_RATIO.

A13 review L5: a code ratio of 1.0 builds ParentBased(TraceIdRatioBased(1)) — an unsampled remote parent stays unsampled. Fails on a regression to bare AlwaysOn, and on OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on winning over the code value.
